title: "Be kind" small hoop in cross-stitch
subtitle: A two-word phrase with a small heart motif in a 10 cm hoop
excerpt: "Be kind" is a compact 50-by-35 stitch piece on 14-count Aida. The two words sit in a clean block alphabet above a small centred heart, all in a single floss colour. It fits in a 10 cm (4 inch) hoop and stitches in a short session.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library.

content.text: "Be kind" is a 50-by-35 stitch piece on 14-count
. A 5-stitch-tall block alphabet gives the two words at the top; a small solid heart sits below, centred. One

colour covers the whole piece. It fits inside a 10 cm (4 inch) hoop with comfortable margin. The design is intentionally simple, it is a good first text project or a quick gift piece that can be completed in a single session.

items.name: 14-count Aida, white or cream
items.substitutions: Pale pink or pale blue Aida suit the sentiment well

items.name: DMC floss
items.qty: 1 skein in your chosen colour, 3831 (raspberry), 3808 (teal), or 823 (navy) are all popular choices

items.name: Round hoop
items.substitutions: A 12 cm (5 inch) hoop works if a wider margin is preferred

content.text: Count the width of "BE KIND" (two words, the space between them is 2 stitches). Mark the centre stitch, this falls in the gap between E and K. Mark the same position on the fabric.
Stitch outward from the centre. The letters are just 5 stitches tall, so even first-time text stitchers should find the count manageable.
Stitch the heart centred below the text, 3 stitches below the baseline. The heart is 11 stitches wide and 10 stitches tall.

Trim the fabric to leave about 3 cm of margin around the hoop inner ring. Secure the excess fabric to the back of the inner hoop with a few stitches or hot glue. Display the hoop as-is or add a ribbon loop for hanging.

items.symptom: The words look crowded and hard to read
items.cause: The gap between the two words was stitched at one square rather than the two-square gap on the chart.
items.fix: Count the gap on the chart: there should be two empty squares between "be" and "kind". Unpick the second word and recount from the chart centre. Once the gap is correct, the text should read clearly at arm's length.

items.symptom: The border circle does not close evenly
items.cause: The border was worked in one direction all the way around rather than in two halves from the top.
items.fix: Work the top half of the circle border first, then count down both sides simultaneously to meet at the base. This keeps the two halves symmetrical. Once the base stitches join, the circle should close without a gap.

content.text: Any two-word phrase that fits in forty or fifty stitches works in this format. "Stay home", "grow wild", "stitch on" are all the right width for a 10 cm hoop.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.
